rationale: Round 0 built and ran correctly with no reported regressions, so this round pushes obfuscation strength up moderately while guarding runtime: Searching-flt is a small, loop-dominated benchmark (14 functions, 43KB text, dominated by the 39KB unrolled `init`), so flattening (FLA) and bogus control flow (BCF) get the highest security weights to disrupt the large straight-line loop bodies that dominate reverse-engineering effort, but their runtime/size cost weights stay elevated so the selector is discouraged from applying them to the hottest inner loops. SUB gets a high DiversityGain with moderate security weight since instruction substitution adds cheap static diversity with low risk on scalar float code. SPLIT stays moderate to fragment the oversized `init` into harder-to-track regions without ballooning the tiny binary. IBR and ICALL are held at mid weights: indirect branching and indirect calls add real disassembly confusion but carry measurable dispatch overhead in tight loops. IGV keeps low cost and good diversity for global-variable indirection, which suits TSVC's heavy use of globals arrays with minimal correctness exposure. All correctness-risk weights remain low-to-moderate since the round-0 build was clean; no pass is disabled to preserve diversity across the feature dimensions.
